title: Concept: Cookie set with SameSite=None in javascript — review required
description: In javascript, a cookie is written with SameSite=None. The attribute exists to permit cross-site delivery, which also means the cookie is attached to requests initiated by other origins. Without the Secure attribute browsers reject it outright; with Secure it still widens the CSRF surface compared with Lax. The decision should be explicit, not a default copied from a tutorial.
applicability: javascript services that set cookies with explicit attributes.
risk: Cross-site request exposure and session misuse; MEDIUM severity.
